Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the afternoon session on Day 3 as the umpires make their way out to the middle. The Australian players get onto the field and take their respective fielding positions while Zak Crawley and Ben Duckett will open the innings for England. Pat Cummins has the new ball in his hand and will begin proceedings. Let's go...
... THIRD INNINGS ...

Australia will have to bowl out of their skins to keep the aggressive England batters in check in the third innings and we expect some entertainment to come our way. Will England score at a rapid rate and take the game away from the Aussies? Or will their plans backfire giving the visitors a golden opportunity to run through their batting order? Do join us at 6.10 pm IST (12.40 GMT) for the second session of Day 3 for more edge-of-the-seat action.

Australia did not try to match England's batting style and started off cautiously on Day 2 having scored 14 runs on Day 1 in four overs. David Warner played a poor shot in the quest to up the ante and lost his wicket to Stuart Broad and Marnus Labuschagne was gone on the very next ball leaving Australia in tatters. Steven Smith stayed on for a while but could not make a substantial score as he was dismissed by Ben Stokes. The middle order stood up for the Aussies and the likes of Travis Head, Cameron Green, and Alex Carey, all made handy contributions and added valuable runs with the centurion Usman Khawaja. Cummins too scored a quick-fire 38 to get Australia closer to the English total but the rest of the tail could not contribute much. Stuart Broad and Ollie Robinson claimed three wickets each with Moeen Ali chipping in with two wicket having bowled a long spell. James Anderson and Ben Stokes claimed one wicket each and England will feel that their gamble to declare early has paid off as the game is well and truly alive.

SESSION SUMMARY- 75 runs, 22.1 overs, 5 wickets. Some terrific bowling just before Lunch by England sees them bundle out Australia for 386, getting a small lead of 7 runs. This has been England’s session all the way and they have staked their advantage in this tie. James Anderson started the day by dismissing Alex Carey with a peach of the delivery. Pat Cummins joined Usman Khawaja out in the middle and the duo looked solid at the crease. They added 34 before Khawaja looked to pick up the scoring rate and was cleaned up by Ollie Robinson. English pacers deployed the short ball tactics against the Aussie tail and they were rewarded instantly as Ollie Robinson claimed two more and Stuart Broad picked up once as well. The last four wickets fell in a hurry and England will want to take this momentum into their batting in the second inning.

OUT! CAUGHT! Australia trail by 7 runs and England will be thrilled with their effort this morning as they have managed to run through the Aussie tail in a jiffy! Ollie Robinson has been the destroyer-in-chief as he has claimed three wickets to give his side a slight advantage in this match. Ollie Robinson bangs this in short and outside the off stump. Pat Cummins is looking for some quick runs and takes on the bouncer with a pull shot but the ball skids through to him quicker than he anticipated. He manages to get a top edge that flies high towards deep mid-wicket. Ben Stokes comes running in from the deep and holds on to the catch to see his side take a slender first-inning lead. That will be Lunch on Day 3!

OUT! TIMBER! This is some outstanding captaincy from Ben Stokes as he continued to manipulate the field and his bowlers have stuck to the task! Ollie Robinson reaps the reward for some disciplined bowling by England and it brings an end to an outstanding inning from Usman Khawaja! The crowd appreciates his effort as he departs 9 runs short of 150 runs. The field is completely unorthodox and Ollie Robinson bowls a pin-point yorker aimed for the off pole. Usman Khawaja looks to pick up the ante and gives the bowler the charge but misses the ball. The stumps are shattered and Australia lose their seventh wicket with Ollie Robinson picking up his first of this game. The hosts will now be hoping to have a go at the Australian tail.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS! Australia have got off to a steady start in the first hour of Day 3 as they have brought down the deficit to just 28 runs and are now in a good position to look for a lead before Lunch. Usman Khawaja has continued along his merry way accumulating runs at will without giving the opponents much of a chance. Alex Carey was dropped early but James Anderson managed to get his first wicket of the game when he shattered the stumps of the wicket-keeper. The Aussies will want the tail to support Khawaja and keep piling on the runs while England will be desperate to bowl the opponents out before this session ends.

Commentary.Commentary: We are set for the start of Day 3 as the umpires are out in the middle. Th English players have taken their respective positions in the field as Usman Khawaja and Alex Carey are ready to continue their partnership. James Anderson has the ball in his hand and will begin proceedings this morning. Let's play...

On the other hand, Australia got off to a shaky start on Day 2 losing David Warner and Marnus Labuschagne in consecutive deliveries. Steven Smith did get himself in but could not carry on as he was caught plumb in front of the wicket and at that point, the visitors looked to be in a spot of bother. However, Usman Khawaja stood firm and forged stands with first Travis Head and then Cameron Green to resurrect the inning. Khawaja stroked his way to a well-compiled hundred and stitched another unbeaten partnership with Alex Carey who managed to reach his fifty. Trailing by 82 runs, the Aussies would want this pair to bat well and take them to parity. Who are you backing to take the first-innings lead? Stick around, as the first ball on Day 3 is not far away.

After taking a bold decision to declare late on Day 1, it was Stuart Broad who set the tone for England on Day 2, striking twice in as many deliveries. Ben Stokes got a crucial wicket even though he was not at his best with the ball and then Moeen Ali picked up two to reduce Australia to 220-5. At that stage, the hosts would have fancied themselves to take a healthy lead but they failed to do so as they were made to toil hard in the field in the last session. Late in the day, Stuart Broad had Usman Khawaja chopping the new ball onto the stumps but he overstepped and gave the centurion a lifeline. The second new ball is 14 overs old but they will be hoping for overcast conditions in the morning to get some movement in the air.

Hello and a warm welcome, ladies and gentlemen, to our coverage of Day 3 of the first Test between England and Australia at the Edgbaston in Birmingham. The first two days of the Test have certainly lived up to expectations with the game ebbing and flowing throughout the six sessions and now that we have arrived on what many consider the moving day of Test cricket, we expect more enthralling action in store for us. The game is evenly poised with both teams aware that one misstep could cost them this game and an early loss in what is a long series.
... DAY 3, SESSION 1 ...

Australia have consolidated their position on Day 2 and will be eager to establish control on Day 3 which is considered the moving day of a Test match. England need some quick wickets to wrench back some control in this match as we look forward to some more excitement. The action continues on Sunday 18th June as we shall have Day 3 of this first Ashes Test which promises to be equally entertaining. The first ball will be bowled at 3.30 pm IST (10.00 am GMT) but do join us early for the build-up. Until then, take care and goodbye!

Australia started the day with all their wickets intact but suffered an early blow as David Warner was dismissed by Stuart Broad for the 15th time and things got better when he dismissed the number one Test batter on the very next delivery to shift the momentum in England’s favor. Usman Khawaja and Steven Smith looked to steady the ship but Ben Stokes dismissed Smith against the run of play and made the first session go completely England’s way. The second session was tilted towards Australia as a quickfire half-century from Travis Head got some life into the Aussie inning. Head could not make it big and was dismissed by Moeen Ali as he looked to keep playing his shots. The sun came out as the day progressed making the conditions better and it become easier for the batters to play their shots. The hosts have lacked the cutting edge and have not got enough purchase from the wicket but credit cannot be taken away from the Australian batters.

SESSION SUMMARY - 123 runs, 33 overs, 1 wicket. Australia have grown through the day and after having a poor first session suddenly find themselves in a good position courtesy of their effort in the second and the final session of Day 2. They have piled on the runs and now trail England by only 82 runs as they will look to get the upper hand on Day 3. They came out to bat after Tea looking to be more positive and Cameron Green looked to play his shots to help his side get some momentum. Usman Khawaja reached his 15th Test century as he added 72 runs for the fifth wicket with Green who was dismissed by Moeen Ali with a peach of a delivery. Alex Carey continued to contribute coming in at number seven and kept the tempo up as he powered towards a commanding half-century. The partnership between the two southpaws has reached 91 runs in 164 balls and if this continues, it could prove to be troublesome for England.

England tried to keep it tight and adopted the short deliveries to attack Travis Head but got a taste of their own medicine as the number 3 Test batter in the world went about his business with positive intent. Moeen Ali toiled hard bowling consistently from one end and was rewarded with a wicket for his effort. The pace bowlers did not get much help from the surface but have not allowed the Australian batters to score freely which has helped them stay ahead of the game. The hosts will know that a few quick wickets in the final session will expose the tail of their opponents and they can wrap up the inning at the earliest. Will they be able to get through Australia's batting line-up in the final session? Or will the visitors continue to battle and claw themselves back into this contest? Do join us at 8.35 pm IST (3.05 pm GMT) for the third and final session of Day 2 for more enticing action.

SESSION SUMMARY - 110 runs, 30 overs, 1 wicket. Austalia have managed to pull things back after a difficult morning session where they lost three wickets. They now trail by 205 runs and a chunk of the credit has to go to Usman Khawaja who has battled it out in the middle and is creeping towards yet another century having scored 84 runs in 176 balls. He had Travis Head for company for almost an hour as the two added 81 runs in 113 deliveries for the fourth wicket but Head looked to continue showing attacking intent and was dismissed as soon as he reached his half-century. Cameron Green joined Khawaja out in the middle and instantly gave England an opportunity as he charged down the wicket but Jonny Bairstow was not able to collect the ball missing a stumping opportunity. He has looked solid after that point in his short inning so far and Australia will be hoping the two of them can get them as close to England’s total as possible.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS! The session was firmly in Austalia's control till the wicket fell before the hour mark. England will want to keep chipping at the wickets while Australia need to start once again and build a partnership that takes them to a position of comfort. Cameron Green joins Usman Khawaja out in the middle and he will have to face spin early in his inning.

OUT! CAUGHT! Moeen Ali's return to the side has been marked with a massive wicket as the man in form Travis Head has to depart right after reaching his half-century! This partnership was building nicely for Australia and just when they were looking to be in cruise-control mode, England got the breakthrough. Moeen Ali floats this one full and into the stumps. Travis Head charges down the wicket and looks to go over the infield but does not connect cleanly and hits this straight to Zak Crawley at mid-wicket. Australia lose their fourth wicket now and England have a timely wicket just before an hour's play in the second session.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the second session of Day 2 as the umpires make their way out to the middle. The English players will have their tails up and they will look to put further dents into the Australian batting order as they disperse to take their respective fielding positions. Usman Khawaja and Travis Head will be eager to bail their side out of trouble with a partnership as they stride out towards the pitch. Moeen Ali has the ball in his hand and will begin proceedings post-Lunch. Let's go...
... DAY 2, SESSION 2 ...

Stuart Broad was the pick of the English bowlers in this session. He bowled tight lines and picked up Warner for the 15th time in his career. He dismissed Labuschagne soon after on the very next ball and reduced Australia to 29 for 2. Ben Stokes came in as the enforcer and removed Australia’s best batter, Smith, at the stroke of Lunch to make this England’s session. Travis Head and Usman Khawaja have a huge task ahead of them to build a strong stand and take Australia into a comfortable position. Will they bail Australia out of trouble or England continue their dominance? We shall find out soon. Join us back at 6.15 pm IST (12.45 pm GMT) for the second session.

SESSION SUMMARY- 64 runs, 27 overs, 3 wickets. The wicket of Steve Smith, just a couple of minutes before the lunch break has tilted the session in England’s favour this morning. Australia started the day with Warner and Khawaja at the crease. England bowled tight lines to them and gave nothing away. Warner was induced into playing a poor shot and chopped a wide delivery onto his stumps to give England their first breakthrough. Marnus Labuschagne was gone soon after for a golden duck as the hosts were all over the Aussies. Smith joined Khawaja in the middle and the duo batted sensibly as they added 38 for the 3rd wicket. Khawaja was the aggressor among the duo as the southpaw got some crisp boundaries away. Smith looked solid at the crease before England skipper Ben Stokes trapped him in front and picked up a huge wicket for his side. England will be the happier side going into the break.

Commentary.Commentary: We are done with the formalities as the umpires walk towards the pitch. The English players take their respective positions on the field as David Warner and Usman Khawaja stride out to the center to resume their opening partnership. Stuart Broad has the ball in his hand and is ready to begin proceedings. Let's play...
Both sets of players line up on the ground along with the umpires and everyone will give a round of applause for 45 seconds in memory of Bob Willis.

It is Blue for Bob Day in honor of former England captain and fast bowler Bob Willis which means Edgbaston will be decked in blue today and the players will don blue caps. Blue for Bob is designed to raise awareness for prostate cancer and encourages people to donate to the cause. Also, there is a slight delay to the start of the game as we will get going 5 minutes later at 3.35 pm IST (10.05 am GMT).

The news from Edgbaston is that we had rain this morning and the covers were on the pitch. It is overcast at the moment and there will definitely be more on offer for the bowlers on Day 2. England will be thrilled as there was very little help from the wicket with the sun glaring down on Day 1 and this could provide the hosts with the perfect opportunity to make their declaration count. Stay tuned as we bring you further updates on the weather as we close in on the morning session of the second day of the first Ashes Test match.

The Australian openers survived the four overs at the end of the day and made 14 runs without losing a wicket. Earlier in the day, Nathan Lyon was the pick of the Aussie bowlers with four wickets to his name, while Hazlewood picked up two scalps. Both teams will be equally happy with their efforts on Day 1. Australia will look to bat well and get over 550 in their first innings to put some pressure back on the Ben Stokes-led side. A thrilling day is in store for us. Stay tuned, as we shall be with you to bring the live action shortly.

England, opting to bat first on a flat pitch at Edgbaston, lost Ben Duckett early in the innings. Zak Crawley looked in sublime touch and added 70 runs for the second wicket with Ollie Pope. Root and Brook carried on the momentum and stitched another half-century stand before Brook was bowled in a rather unlucky manner. Stokes followed him soon after, and England were struggling at 176 for 5. Bairstow came in and steadied the ship with Root by adding 121 runs in quick time. Root added valuable runs with the lower order and notched up his 30th Test ton. He remained unbeaten on 118 before England decided to declare.

Hello and a warm welcome to our coverage of Day 2 in this first Test between England and Australia at the Edgbaston in Birmingham. England carried on their attacking brand of cricket and scored 393 in just 78 overs. Ben Stokes made a bold decision to declare and have a bowl at the Aussies. England could have easily gotten close to 450 in their first innings, but their change in mindset and approach, since Stokes took over, wouldn’t have surprised many. We witnessed an entertaining Day 1 in the Ashes, and Day 2 promises to be equally exciting.
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ...

England have kept up with their recent reputation and have played with positive intent through Day 1 with the declaration coming as a show of strength by Ben Stokes. This could easily backfire if Australia manage to consolidate their position on Day 2 with the bat and it could easily take the game away from the hosts. The action continues on Saturday 17th June as we shall have Day 2 of this first Ashes Test which promises to be equally entertaining. The first ball will be bowled at 3.30 pm IST (10.00 am GMT) but do join us early for the build-up. Until then, take care and goodbye!

Australia looked completely shaken by the Jonny Bairstow onslaught as the 121-run partnership for the sixth wicket which came in just 140 deliveries threatened to take the game away from them. They lacked any sort of plans and when Alex Carey dropped Bairstow behind the stumps, it looked like Australia were in for a long day. That was not the case though as the English batters decided to self-destruct and Nathan Lyon got two of them stumped trying to send him out of the ground. The deceleration by England meant that he missed out on another five-wicket haul and he had to settle with four wickets. Cameron Green disturbed Stuart Broad’s stumps and got his first wicket of the game. They had a long day in the office with all the batters going after them barring Joe Root who showed his class with a well-constructed inning but they kept chipping away at the wickets. They would have not expected to bat though but David Warner and Usman Khawaja handled the pressure well and went into Stumps unscathed as they trail by 379 runs which puts them in a better position going into Day 2.

SESSION SUMMARY - 167 runs, 30 overs, 3 wickets. England continued from where they left off at Tea break as they came out into the final session looking to play their shots and accumulate the runs. Jonny Bairstow looked to be at his dominating best as he scored freely and reached his half-century in his comeback Test. His aggression brought about his downfall as he looked to charge the spinner and was stumped having scored a run a ball 78. Moeen Ali came out to the middle and looked to continue the onslaught and scored a quickfire 18 but became the second England batter who found himself stranded well out of the crease. Stuart Broad looked comfortable at the wicket and just when it looked like he would play the supporting role to Joe Root, he played a rash shot and saw his stumps shattered. Root continued to accumulate runs on the other end though and reached his 30th Test century with Ollie Robinson doing a good job to give him company. With 393 runs on the board, England decided to have a go at the Australian openers but were unable to get a breakthrough in the 4 overs that they bowled.
